onboarding.title: Get your farm set up
onboarding.subtitle: A few quick steps to get the most out of FleetWise.
onboarding.allDone: You're all set up — nice work!
onboarding.step1Desc: Add each tractor, bakkie, harvester and implement — or import them all from a spreadsheet.
onboarding.step2Desc: Apply a service template to each machine so FleetWise knows when a service is due.
onboarding.step3Desc: Print a QR sticker for each machine and stick it on. This is the bit that makes the whole thing work — anyone who can hold a phone can then report a problem or write down the hours, with no login.
onboarding.step4Desc: Add your manager and mechanic so job cards and faults are captured as work happens.
onboarding.step3Hint: Print them on plain paper and tape them somewhere dry — inside the cab door works well.

tour.welcomeBody: This keeps track of every machine on the farm — when it was serviced, what broke, and what it cost you. Six short steps and you will know your way around. You can stop at any time.
tour.machinesBody: Every tractor, bakkie, harvester and implement goes in here once. If you already have a list on a spreadsheet, import it instead of typing it again.
tour.qrBody: Each machine gets a sticker. Anyone can hold a phone to it and report a problem or write down the hours — no login, no account, no training. This is the step that makes the rest of FleetWise work on its own.
tour.faultsBody: Problems reported from the stickers land here, worst first. You turn one into a job card when someone is going to work on it.
tour.jobcardsBody: A job card records what was done to a machine — the parts, the hours and the cost. Approve it when the work is finished and it locks, so the cost history stays honest.
tour.moneyBody: Everything above adds up here: cost per machine, per hour, per kilometre, and which machines break most often. This is the part that pays for itself.
tour.installBody: Install FleetWise so it opens from the home screen and keeps working in a shed or a far land. Whatever is captured without signal is sent on its own when the signal comes back.
tour.helpBody: Every screen has a “What is this?” button next to its name that explains what the screen is for. You can start this walkthrough again from there whenever you like.
tour.driverWelcomeBody: This is for the people who work on the machines. Four things, no paperwork. It takes a minute to show you.
tour.driverScanTitle: Hold your phone to the sticker
tour.driverScanBody: Every machine has a sticker on it. Hold your phone to it and the machine comes up on the screen — you do not have to log in or find it in a list.
tour.driverFaultBody: Broken, leaking, or making a noise — press one button, take a photo if it helps, and the farm office sees it. You can talk into it instead of typing.
tour.driverHoursBody: Read the number off the clock and type it in. That is what tells the office when the machine is due for a service, so it does not break in the middle of a season.
tour.contractorWelcomeBody: Every farm you work for sends you jobs in one place, so you are not chasing five different WhatsApp groups. A minute to show you around.
tour.contractorWorkTitle: All your jobs, all your farms
tour.contractorWorkBody: New requests arrive here with the vehicle, what is wrong and how urgent it is. One list across every farm that has connected you.
tour.contractorQuoteBody: Send a price from inside the job. When the farmer accepts it you do the work, then send the invoice from the same screen. You can call or WhatsApp them without leaving it.
tour.contractorDocumentsBody: Build a quote line by line and send it, turn an accepted quote into an invoice, and record payments as they land. Already invoice somewhere else? Attach that document instead — it works on every plan.
tour.contractorBrandBody: Your name, registration and VAT numbers, banking details, logo and colours. Everything you send goes out on your letterhead, not ours.

correct.title: Something wrong with this one?
correct.intro: Sent documents stay as they are — that is what makes them a record. Here is how you fix a mistake without pretending it never happened.
correct.reasonHint: Shown on the credit note, so your customer knows why.
correct.shouldNotExist: It should never have gone out
correct.shouldNotExistHint: Wrong customer, or a duplicate. The document and its number stay on file; the money comes off.
correct.voidBody: This stops the money counting. The document stays on file with your reason on it, so anyone looking later can see what happened.
correct.voidConsequence1: It comes off what the customer owes you.
correct.voidConsequence2: If a copy is already out there, it will still say cancelled when they open the link.
correct.voidReasonHint: A few words is enough. This is what you will read in six months.
correct.overchargedHint: A credit note puts the money back. Use this when they have already paid — the refund needs to show as its own thing.
correct.underchargedHint: A debit note adds the difference to the same job, so it reads as part of that invoice on their statement instead of turning up as a mystery charge.
correct.neverPaying: They are never going to pay
correct.neverPayingHint: Write it off. The invoice stays on their statement exactly as it was — the work was done — but it stops counting as money you are owed, and we stop chasing it.
correct.writeOffBody: Use this when you have given up on collecting. It is not the same as cancelling — the bill was correct, the money is just not coming.

stage.partOfBody: This invoice bills part of a quote. Here is where it sits in the whole job.

recurring.title: Standing invoices
recurring.lead: Bills that go out on the same day every month without you having to remember.
recurring.dueBody: These will be raised on tonight’s run. Open one to raise it now instead.
recurring.name: What do you call this?
recurring.nameHint: Only you see this — for example: Weltevrede monthly service contract.
recurring.subject: What should the invoice say it is for?
recurring.notes: Anything to put on the invoice?
recurring.autoSendHint: Off means we make a draft and tell you, so you can look before the customer does.
recurring.noLines: This has nothing on it yet, so nothing will go out. Add a line below.
recurring.runNowBody: This does exactly what tonight’s run would do, just sooner.
recurring.runNowSends: It will be sent to the customer straight away.
recurring.runNowDrafts: It will be made as a draft for you to check first.
recurring.runNowIdempotent: If this period has already been billed, nothing happens — you cannot bill twice by accident.
recurring.nothingFlash: Nothing to raise — this period has already been billed.
recurring.deleteConsequence: Invoices it has already raised stay exactly as they are.
recurring.emptyBody: If you bill someone the same amount every month, set it up once here and stop remembering it.
recurring.footnote: These are raised overnight. If one is due today it will go out tonight.

layout.title: How your documents look
layout.lead: The wording and the blocks on every quote and invoice you send. Change it once; it applies to everything from now on.
layout.namesBody: Leave any of these empty to use the normal wording.
layout.invoiceTitleHint: If you are registered for VAT this needs to say “tax invoice” somewhere, or your customer’s accountant will send it back.
layout.showUnitPriceHint: Turn this off to show only the line total — some trades prefer it.
layout.densityCompact: Tight — fits more on a page
layout.savedFlash: Saved. New documents will use this.
layout.frozenNote: Documents you have already sent keep the look they were sent with — changing this cannot restate an old invoice.

stock.storeLead: What is actually on the shelf. Receiving and issuing keeps the count right — the number is worked out from those, never typed.
stock.emptyBody: Press "Track in store" on a part below to start counting it.
stock.untrackConsequence: The part stays in the catalogue and the history of what was fitted stays. Only the shelf count goes.

money.title: Money
money.lead: Did it make money, who owes you, and who you owe.
money.basis: Counted when you invoiced, not when you were paid.
money.blockedVat: of that, VAT you cannot claim back
money.cashHint: Actually banked and paid in this period
money.owedNoneBody: Every invoice you have sent has been settled.
money.owingNoneBody: Every supplier invoice you have captured is marked paid.
money.owingAgeNote: Counted from the date on the supplier invoice — a supplier invoice carries no due date.
money.quotesDecidedHint: Of the ones that actually got an answer: {rate}
money.quotesExpiredNote: A quote counts as expired once its valid-until date has passed, whether or not the overnight job has caught up with it.

po.cancelConsequence: The supplier is not sending it. No money was ever owed on it.
po.cancelKeeps: The record of what you nearly bought stays.
po.claimable: I can claim this VAT back
po.claimableHint: Entertainment, a passenger car and club fees carry VAT you may not claim.
po.closeConsequence: It stops showing as outstanding. Everything on it is kept.
po.closeIntro: Use this when nothing more is coming from the supplier.
po.convertedFlash: The supplier invoice is on your books.
po.createdFlash: Order started. Now say what you are buying.
po.deleteConsequence: It disappears from your order list.
po.deletePrefer: If the supplier simply is not sending it, cancel it instead — that keeps the history.
po.emptyBody: Write down what you have ordered, and you will know what is still coming and what arrived short.

err.alreadyConverted: This order's invoice is already on the books. Only one invoice can be captured against an order.
err.badStatus: That is not something you set by hand — what arrives decides it.
err.cannotConvert: Send the order first, or put it back to draft if it was cancelled.
err.failed: That did not save. Please try again.
err.hasExpense: The supplier's invoice is captured against this order, so it cannot be removed. Cancel it instead.
err.needSupplier: Say who you are ordering from.
err.notFound: That order is not there any more.

po.expectedHint: When they said it would arrive.
po.inclVat: The amount I typed includes VAT
po.invoiceDateHint: The date on their invoice, not today.
po.invoiceHint: Ordering costs nothing. Capture their invoice here and it goes onto your books once — your VAT return and your profit pick it up from there.
po.invoiceNotYet: Send the order first. An invoice can only be captured once the order is with the supplier.
po.invoiceNumberHint: The number on the paper they sent.
po.lateWarning: This was due already. Worth a phone call.
po.lead: What you have ordered and not yet been invoiced for.
po.lessThanOrdered: That is less than the order by
po.lineDescriptionHint: In your own words — the supplier's description is fine.
po.lineInclVat: The price I typed includes VAT
po.lineQtyHint: Litres and metres are fine too.
po.lineRemoveTotals: The order's total changes to match.
po.linesEmptyBody: Add each thing you are buying, with the price you were quoted.
po.moreThanOrdered: That is more than the order by
po.newHint: Start with who it is with. You say what you are buying on the next screen.
po.notesHint: Anything worth remembering about this order.
po.referenceHint: The number you give them on the phone.
po.seeInExpenses: See it with your other expenses
po.supplierVatHint: SARS wants it on a claim over R5 000.
po.title: Purchase orders
po.vatAmountHint: Leave this as it is unless their invoice says something different.
po.vatPercentHint: What the supplier will add. Use 0 if they charge none.

bank.accountLabelHint: So you can tell this statement from the others later — "Cheque account", "Credit card".
bank.allClearBody: Every line on your statement has been matched or set aside.
bank.alreadyFlash: That one was already done — nothing was recorded twice.
bank.confirmInConsequence: The invoice is credited with this amount and its status moves on its own.
bank.confirmOutConsequence: The supplier invoice is marked paid on the date the money left.
bank.emptyBody: Download a CSV from your internet banking and load it here. We will show you which invoices and supplier bills each line looks like, and you decide.

err.already_settled: That invoice is already fully paid.
err.empty: That file has nothing in it.
err.missing_amount: We could not find an amount. Pick either one signed amount column, or the money-in and money-out pair.
err.missing_date: We could not find a date column. Go back and pick which column holds the transaction date.
err.more_than_owed: This payment is more than the invoice still owes. Record it on the invoice itself so the difference is visible.
err.not_an_invoice: That document is not an invoice.
err.not_found: That line is no longer there.
err.nothing_valid: Nothing in that file could be read as a transaction. Check the column matching.
err.too_many: That is more than {n} lines. Load one statement period at a time.
err.wrong_direction: Money going one way cannot settle something going the other way.

bank.importIntro: Export your account as a CSV and choose the file. Any bank's layout works — you check the columns on the next step.
bank.importLead: A CSV from your internet banking. We match your columns to ours before anything is stored.
bank.importedFlash: {n} new lines loaded, out of {seen} on the statement.
bank.lead: Load your bank statement and tick off what has been paid.
bank.mapBalanceNote: Leave the running balance out — it is not a transaction.
bank.mapHint: We guessed from the headings. The value underneath each one is from your file — check it looks right.
bank.mapNoAmount: No amount is matched. Pick either one signed amount column, or the money-in and money-out pair.
bank.mapNoDate: No date column is matched. Pick which of your columns holds the transaction date.
bank.noSuggestionsIn: Nothing here looks like this payment. Check the invoice was sent, or record it on the invoice itself.
bank.noSuggestionsOut: No unpaid supplier invoice matches this. Capture it under Expenses first if it is a purchase.
bank.reimportSafe: Safe to load the same statement twice — lines already here are left alone.
bank.removeConsequence1: It disappears from the bank list. Nothing in your books changes.
bank.removeConsequence2: It will not come back when you load the same statement again.
bank.setAsideNote: Set aside — bank charges, transfers, anything that will never match here.
bank.statOpenOutHint: bills that may already be settled
bank.title: Bank
bank.undoConsequence1: The payment is reversed and the invoice goes back to what it was owed.
bank.undoConsequence2: The bank line comes back to the list so it can be matched again.
bank.undoneFlash: Undone. The line is back on the list.

why.amountExact: the amount is exactly what is owed
why.amountTotal: the amount is the invoice total
why.name: the name is on the statement
why.reference: the reference is on the statement
why.referenceDigits: the number appears on the statement

supplier.accountNumberHint: The number you quote on the phone.
supplier.contactHint: The person who answers, not the switchboard.
supplier.deleteConsequence1: Their invoices stay exactly as they are. Nothing about the money changes.
supplier.deleteConsequence2: Those invoices go back to being grouped by the name typed on them, so what you owe may split across spellings again.
supplier.deleteFootnote: Nothing is really erased. If you have simply stopped buying from them, use "Stop using" instead — it keeps everything and only takes them off the list.
supplier.emptyBody: Add the businesses you buy from. Every invoice you capture in their name is then filed against them, and what you owe each one shows as a single line instead of one line per spelling.
supplier.errDuplicate: You already have a supplier by that name.
supplier.errNotFound: That supplier could not be found.
supplier.lead: The businesses you buy from, and what you still owe each one.
supplier.name: Business name
supplier.noTerms: No terms or account number on file.
supplier.pickHint: Pick one so this invoice is filed against them.
supplier.statUnfiledHint: Filed under a typed name only
supplier.termsHint: Leave empty if you pay on collection.
supplier.title: Suppliers
supplier.unfiledNote: Some invoices are still filed under a typed name only. Add that business above and they attach to it. Nothing is created for you, because then a typo would become a supplier.
supplier.vatNumberHint: Needed on a claim over R5 000.

recexp.autoPaid: It goes off by itself — debit order or stop order
recexp.autoPaidHint: Then it is recorded as already paid on the day. Leave it off and it sits on your creditors list until you say it was paid.
recexp.captureNowBody: This writes an ordinary expense for the period that is due, exactly as tonight's run would.
recexp.captureNowIdempotent: If this period has already been captured, nothing happens. The same month cannot be booked twice.
recexp.captureNowOwing: It stays on your creditors list until you say it was paid.
recexp.captureNowPaid: It is recorded as already paid.
recexp.capturedFlash: Captured. It is in your expenses, your VAT return and your profit figure now.
recexp.claimable: I can claim this VAT back
recexp.claimableHint: Untick it for entertainment, a passenger vehicle or club fees — SARS does not refund that VAT (VAT Act s17(2)). On a standing cost it applies every single month.
recexp.committed: Over a year these come to
recexp.deleteConsequence: Nothing will be captured for it again.
recexp.deleteKeepsHistory: Expenses already captured stay exactly where they are. They were real costs, and removing them would change a VAT period you may already have filed.
recexp.descriptionHint: What appears on the expense itself. Leave it empty to use the name above.
recexp.dueBody: These get captured on tonight's run. Together they come to
recexp.emptyBody: Rent, insurance, salaries, the monthly parts account, the accountant's fee. Set each one up once and it is captured every month without anybody remembering.
recexp.endsOnHint: Leave it empty if it just carries on.
recexp.errNeedAmount: Enter an amount greater than zero.
recexp.errNeedName: Give the standing cost a name.
recexp.errNotFound: That standing cost no longer exists.
recexp.footnote: The nightly run captures every standing cost that is due. It cannot capture the same period twice, so a retry, a double-fired run and a press of "Capture it now" all leave you with one expense for the month.
recexp.lead: Rent, insurance, salaries, the monthly account — the bills that come whether anybody remembers them or not. Set one up once and it gets captured for you.
recexp.name: What to call it
recexp.nameHint: Your own name for it, like "Workshop rent".
recexp.notClaimableNote: This VAT is not claimed back. It still counts as money spent, so it shows up as a cost rather than as input VAT.
recexp.nothingFlash: Nothing to capture — this period has already been done.
recexp.referenceHint: Whatever appears on the monthly bill.
recexp.supplierHint: Just the name. You do not have to file a supplier first.
recexp.supplierVatHint: Needed on a claim over R5 000.
recexp.title: Standing costs
recexp.viewInExpenses: See it with your other expenses
recexp.claimableNotRegistered: You are not registered for VAT, so this VAT counts as part of the cost rather than something to claim back.

cash.grossNote: Every amount here is what actually moves through the bank, VAT included. The ex-VAT figures are on the money screen.
cash.lead: What is coming in and going out, and when.
cash.noOpening: Tell us what is in the bank today and we will show you the week the money runs out.
cash.noneBody: No unpaid invoices, no standing invoices due, and nothing owed to suppliers in this window.
cash.openingBad: That is not an amount we can read. Try 12500 or 12500.50.
cash.openingHint: Optional. Type what is in the account and we work out the balance at each step.
cash.runsOutWarning: On this forecast you run short {bucket}: the balance goes to {amount}.
cash.staysPositive: You stay in the black right through, ending on {amount}.
cash.tableCaption: Money expected in and out, by when it is expected.
cash.termsNote: Supplier bills are assumed to be paid {days} days after the supplier's own invoice date. They carry no due date, so this is an assumption, not a fact.
cash.title: Cash flow
cash.undatedNote: Orders with no expected delivery date are left out: they cannot be put on a calendar.
cash.termsFiled: Bills use each supplier’s own payment terms where you have filed them.

credit.title: Credit
credit.over: They are {amount} over the limit you set for them.
credit.advisory: This is a guide for you, not a block. FleetWise will still let you quote and invoice this customer.

supplierStatement.termsAssumed: No terms on file — 30 days assumed
supplierStatement.ageingHint: Counted from the date on each of their invoices. A supplier invoice does not carry a due date, so this is how long you have been sitting on it — not how late you are.
supplierStatement.grossHint: Every amount includes VAT. This is money that leaves your bank, so it is the same figure the money screen shows.
supplierStatement.emptyBody: No invoices from them and no payments to them between these dates. Try a wider period — anything older is already inside the balance brought forward.
supplierStatement.dueHint: "Due by" is worked out from their payment terms; it is not printed on their invoice. Where you have not filed a term, 30 days is assumed — the same rule the cash-flow screen uses.
supplierStatement.remitLead: Send this with the payment so they know which of their invoices it covers. Without one a supplier usually settles the oldest invoice and then chases you for money you have already sent.
supplierStatement.remitNoneInPeriod: Nothing was paid to this supplier in this period. Pick a wider period, or type the payment date below.
supplierStatement.remitDateHint: The day the money left your bank.
supplierStatement.remitEmpty: No invoices from this supplier are marked paid on that date.
supplierStatement.remitMany: {n} invoices settled by one payment, total

docTemplate.title: Pick the document you send
docTemplate.lead: Four documents, all of them yours. Pick the one that looks right and everything you send from now on uses it.
docTemplate.keepsNote: Your name, logo, colours, standing terms, footer and numbering apply to all four — picking one never throws them away.
docTemplate.changedByHand: You have changed some of the settings below by hand since choosing this.
docTemplate.savedFlash: Saved. Everything you send from now on uses this one.
docTemplate.frozenNote: Anything you have already sent keeps the look it was sent with — picking a different one cannot restate an old invoice.

desc.classic: Your name and colour across the top, roomy rows, and a price against every line. What most workshops send.
desc.compact: Tighter rows, numbered lines, and a thin colour stripe instead of a band. A long job lands on one page instead of two.
desc.plain: No colour anywhere, and a line to sign. Photocopies and faxes cleanly, and prints in black and white without going grey.
desc.totals_only: Says what you did and what each item came to, but keeps your rate per hour and per part off the page.

reorder.title: What the next services need
reorder.window: Counting every service due in the next {days} days.
reorder.headline: {count} parts will run out before the services due in the next {days} days
reorder.allCovered: You have enough of everything these services need.
reorder.nothingDueTitle: No services due in this window
reorder.nothingDueBody: Nothing on the service schedule falls inside the window, so nothing on the shelf is spoken for yet. Give a vehicle a service kit and the parts it needs will show up here.
reorder.severalKitsNote: A vehicle with more than one service kit counts all of them, because nothing here records which kit belongs to which service. Rather more than less.
reorder.windowLabel: How many days ahead to look
reorder.windowHint: Between 1 and 365. Everything above counts services due inside this many days.

packs.scopeFleet: {n} vehicles on hand ({excluded} retired or sold, excluded)
packs.aboutBody: Every figure in this document comes from this farm's own records in FleetWise, as they stood on the date above. It also lists what is NOT on file: where a record is missing, it is named in words rather than left blank, so an empty line is never read as a requirement that was met. The section "What is not on file" at the end is the complete list.
packs.complianceSubtitle: Machinery evidence for a GLOBALG.A.P. / SIZA audit
packs.saleSubtitle: The record that goes with this vehicle when it changes hands
packs.warrantySubtitle: The terms on file, and the evidence the service plan was followed
packs.faultsTitle: Faults reported, and how they ended
packs.noLicenceOnFileOne: No licence or renewal is on file for this vehicle.
packs.noPlanOnFileOne: No service plan is on file for this vehicle, so there is nothing to measure adherence against.
packs.noAssets: No vehicles are on file for this farm.
packs.noJobCards: No job cards are on file for this vehicle.
packs.noReadings: No meter readings are on file for this vehicle.
packs.noPhotos: No photographs are on file for this vehicle.
packs.noCosts: No costs have been recorded against this vehicle.
packs.faultsIntro: An auditor is not asking whether there are faults — every farm has faults. What is being asked is whether a reported fault reaches a conclusion. Resolved faults are therefore listed here too, with the date they closed.
packs.operatorsIntro: Who each vehicle is assigned to, and who has actually driven it recently.
packs.meterHistoryIntro: The most recent readings on file, newest first.
packs.photosIntro: {n} photographs are held against this vehicle. The images are not reproduced in this document — ask for them, or open the vehicle in FleetWise.
packs.declaredFaultsIntro: {n} fault(s) were open on this vehicle when this pack was produced. They are declared here rather than left for the buyer to find.
packs.declaredFaultsNone: No faults were open on this vehicle on {date}.
packs.resolvedFaultsCount: {n} fault(s) have been reported and resolved over the life of this vehicle.
packs.saleBasis: This pack states the records held on {date}. It is a record, not a warranty, and it does not replace an inspection.
packs.costGated: Lifetime cost and total cost of ownership are a Professional feature, and this farm is on a plan that does not include them. The figures exist in the farm's records — this document simply does not print them. Do not read this section as a vehicle that has cost nothing.
packs.adherenceClean: Every task on the plan is up to date, and each one has been done at least once.
packs.adherenceQualified: The plan is not fully up to date. The table below states where each task stands. A warranty claim usually turns on exactly this, so it is stated rather than summarised away.
packs.gapsIntro: The records below were not on file when this pack was produced. They are named so that an absent record is never read as a requirement that was met.
packs.gapsNone: Nothing is missing. Every record this pack looks for was on file.
packs.gapNoLicence: No licence or renewal on file: {machines}.
packs.gapStaleMeter: Meter not read in the last {days} days, so the hours shown are not current: {machines}.
packs.saleGapNoLicence: No licence or renewal is on file for this vehicle.
packs.saleGapNoPurchase: No purchase date or purchase price is on file.
packs.saleGapNoPlan: No service plan is on file, so the service intervals cannot be shown.
packs.saleGapNoHistory: No job cards are on file, so there is no recorded service history to show a buyer.
packs.saleGapNoReadings: No meter readings are on file, so the hours or kilometres cannot be evidenced.
packs.saleGapNoSerial: No serial or VIN number is on file.
packs.saleGapCostsGated: Lifetime cost and total cost of ownership are not printed — they are a Professional feature and this farm is on a lower plan.
packs.warrantyGapNoTerms: No warranty terms are on file — neither an expiry date nor an expiry meter reading.
packs.warrantyGapNoPlan: No service plan is on file, so adherence to it cannot be evidenced.
packs.warrantyGapNoServices: No scheduled service has been recorded on a job card.
packs.warrantyGapNoReadings: No meter readings are on file, so the hours cannot be evidenced.
packs.warrantyGapNoSerial: No serial or VIN number is on file. A manufacturer will ask for it.
packs.warrantyGapNeverDone: Tasks on the plan that have never been done: {tasks}.

accounting.title: Accounting export
accounting.lead: Hand your books to your accountant as a general journal.
accounting.leadFor: The books of {name}, as a general journal your accountant can import.
accounting.genericTitle: This is a generic journal, on purpose
accounting.genericBody: It is not a Sage file or a Xero file. We could not confirm either package's current import columns from the vendors themselves, and a file with the wrong columns does not fail here — it fails at your accountant's desk months later.
accounting.genericHow: Every accounting package can import a journal like this. Your accountant maps the columns once, the first time, and every export after that goes straight in.
accounting.basisNote: Sales are dated when the invoice was issued, not when it was paid. Purchases are dated from the supplier's own invoice.
accounting.emptyTitle: Nothing to export for this period
accounting.emptyHint: Once you have sent an invoice, taken a payment or captured a purchase, it will appear here.
accounting.balanced: Every entry balances — debits equal credits, on each entry and overall.
accounting.unbalanced: {count} entries do not balance. Do not send this file — tell us before you do.
accounting.layoutBody: Two layouts, because packages differ. Pick the one your accountant's software asks for; the numbers are identical.
accounting.chartBody: These are our default codes. Your accountant maps them to your own chart the first time — that is the one-off job, and this list is what they need to do it.

reportSchedules.title: Reports sent to you
reportSchedules.lead: Have a report built and emailed on a schedule, so nobody has to remember to open it.
reportSchedules.addBody: Pick the report, how often it should go out, and who should get it. You can pause or change it at any time.
reportSchedules.name: Name
reportSchedules.nameHint: Something you will recognise in a list, like "Monthly costs for the bank".
reportSchedules.formatHint: PDF reads like a printed page. CSV and Excel open in a spreadsheet.
reportSchedules.startOnHint: The first send happens on or after this date.
reportSchedules.endsOnHint: Leave empty to keep going until you pause it.
reportSchedules.siteHint: Only machines at this site are counted. Leave on all sites to cover the whole farm.
reportSchedules.writtenInHint: The language the report itself is written in. Each person still reads the app in their own.
reportSchedules.whoBody: Add the people on your team who should receive it, or type an address for somebody outside the farm.
reportSchedules.addPersonHint: They receive it at the email address on their profile.
reportSchedules.addEmailHint: For an accountant or a bank — anyone without a FleetWise login.
reportSchedules.noAddress: No email address on their profile
reportSchedules.noRecipients: Nobody yet — this will not send until somebody is added.
reportSchedules.everyoneAdded: Everyone on the team is already on this schedule.
reportSchedules.removeWhoBody: They stop receiving this report. Anything already sent is unaffected.
reportSchedules.dueBody: These are ready for the next nightly run. You can send one early if you need it now.
reportSchedules.nextRunHint: Reports go out overnight, so this is the morning it lands.
reportSchedules.finishedBody: This schedule has passed its end date and will not send again.
reportSchedules.historyEmptyHint: Once the first one goes out you will see it here, with who received it.
reportSchedules.sendNowBody: It is built and emailed immediately to everyone on the list.
reportSchedules.sendNowIdempotent: The scheduled send is not skipped — this is an extra copy, not a replacement.
reportSchedules.pausedBody: Nothing sends while it is paused. Resume whenever you like.
reportSchedules.deleteBody: It stops sending and disappears from your list.
reportSchedules.deleteFootnote: Reports already sent are not affected — this only stops future ones.
reportSchedules.emptyBody: Set one up and the report arrives by email without anyone opening the app.
reportSchedules.nothingDueFlash: Nothing was due, so nothing was sent.

reportEmail.greeting: Here is the report you asked us to send.
reportEmail.includesInactive: Retired and sold machines are included.
reportEmail.excludesInactive: Retired and sold machines are left out.
reportEmail.empty: There was nothing to report for this period, so nothing is attached.
reportEmail.stop: To change or stop this, open Reports in FleetWise and go to your schedules.
reportEmail.footer: Sent automatically by FleetWise. Nobody had to open the app.
